post.description:
One recently funded startup's profile and venture funding, when Fireround holds it: its headquarters (location), its sector, what the company does, its total raised (announced and reported rounds), its valuation (latest and every stated one), every round newest first with its leads and official announcement, and every investor on them, leads first. Use for questions like "where is TypeSafe AI headquartered and what does it do", "tell me about Supabase's funding", "what is Ramp valued at" or "who has invested in Ramp". Takes the company's domain or its id from companies/search. Coverage limit: Fireround tracks rounds announced from 2026 onward. It holds a few thousand companies, most of them startups that raised in 2026, and earlier rounds only for some of those. Most companies, and most rounds before 2026, are not on record, so a lookup of an arbitrary company's full funding history, its pre-2026 rounds, an investor's whole portfolio or acquisitions usually returns nothing here; use a company-data provider with historical funding coverage for those.

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

200.description:
One company's profile and funding: where it is headquartered, its sector, what it does, its total raised, its valuations, every round and every investor.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The company's id: pass it to companies/profile. |
| `name` | string |  |
| `domain` | string | The company's own website, bare, when known. |
| `url` | string | The company's page on fireround.dev, with every round and its sources. |
| `description` | string | What the company does, from its own homepage when read. |
| `sector` | string | The company's sector, as fireround classifies it. |
| `headquarters` | string | Where the company is based, for example `London, UK`. |
| `total_raised_usd_millions` | number | What it raised in million USD: the stated amounts of its announced and reported rounds, never expected or unconfirmed ones. |
| `stated_total_raised` | object | The company's own stated funding to date, from its newest announced or reported round that states one; null when none does. usd_millions, as_written, quote (the sentence that states it), stated_on, stage, stage_as_written, source (the page it is read from), rounds_sum_usd_millions (what its rounds on record add up to by then) and exceeds_rounds_sum (true when the stated total is more than 2% above that sum, so some earlier rounds are missing here). Prefer it to total_raised_usd_millions for "how much has X raised" when exceeds_rounds_sum is true. |
| `valuation_history` | object | What it was valued at, kept apart from what it raised: `stated` lists every round that carries a valuation, newest first (usd_millions, as_written, basis, announced_on, stage, stage_as_written, certainty), and `latest` is the first of them, null when no source states one. |
| `latest_round` | object | Its newest round: stage, stage_as_written, amount (usd_millions, as_written), valuation (usd_millions, as_written, basis: post, pre or unknown; null when no source states one), announced_on, certainty, lead_investors, other_investors, primary_source (the official announcement's URL, or null), earlier_round. |
| `rounds` | object[] | Every round on record, newest first: stage, stage_as_written, amount (usd_millions, as_written), valuation (usd_millions, as_written, basis: post, pre or unknown; null when no source states one), announced_on, certainty, lead_investors, other_investors, primary_source (the official announcement's URL, or null), earlier_round. |
| `investors` | object[] | The investors on its rounds, leads first: id (pass it to investors/profile), name, domain, url, rounds_led, rounds_participated. |

200.description:
One page of rounds under `data`, with `next_cursor` beside it (null on the last page). When a name matched nothing, `did_you_mean` lists up to three near names (`id`, `name`) to retry with. Each round is what Fireround checked: the company, stage, money, valuation when stated, date, certainty, investors, the sentence that states it and the pages it was read from.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `data` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Stable round id, company_key:stage:announced_on. |
| `url` | string | The round's company page on fireround.dev, with every source and the evidence for each field. |
| `company` | object | name, domain, website, description, sector, headquarters. |
| `stage` | string | One of pre_seed, seed, pre_a, series_a, series_b, series_c, series_d_plus, growth, bridge, debt, grant, convertible, secondary, undisclosed, other. |
| `stage_as_written` | string | The stage as the source wrote it, for example `Series B-2`. |
| `amount` | object | usd_millions (null when undisclosed or unconvertible), as_written, currency. |
| `valuation` | string | The post- or pre-money valuation as written, when a source states it. |
| `valuation_disclosed` | boolean | true when a valuation is stated; false when a source says outright that it was not disclosed; null when no source says either way. A null valuation with false here is a known non-disclosure, not a gap. |
| `total_as_written` | string | A larger figure stated beside the round, such as funding to date or the whole financing; never the round's own amount. |
| `announced_on` | string | YYYY-MM-DD; read with date_precision (day, week, month, unknown). |
| `date_precision` | string |  |
| `certainty` | string | announced (closed on the record), reported (said to have closed, citing unnamed sources), expected (still being raised), or unconfirmed (reported or expected, and never confirmed). |
| `verified` | boolean | True when a model read the round back against its sources and they agreed, with any field it corrected applied. |
| `provisional` | boolean | True when the round is public but carries a recorded doubt (thin evidence, low confidence, or no stated amount); treat it as provisional. |
| `earlier_round` | boolean | True for an earlier round of the company, verified on its own, rather than recent news. |
| `is_extension` | boolean | True for an extension of an earlier round. |
| `lead_investors` | string[] |  |
| `other_investors` | string[] |  |
| `evidence` | string | The sentence from a source that states the round. |
| `primary_source` | object | The round's official announcement: url, and kind (company for the company's own page, wire for its newswire release). Null when the sources hold neither. |
| `sources` | object[] | Up to 3 pages the round was read from, in reading order (the official announcement first, then established outlets, then the rest): url, title, publisher, published. |
| `source_count` | number | How many pages the round was read from in all. |
| `trending` | object | While the round is in its first 72 hours: rank, people_on_x, outlets, hn_points. Null after. |
| `previous_rounds` | object[] | The company's other rounds announced before this one, newest first, up to 5: id, stage, stage_as_written, amount (usd_millions, as_written), announced_on, lead_investors, url (the round's official announcement when it has one). |

post.description:
Search startup funding rounds: the latest rounds, the biggest rounds, and rounds by stage, sector, investor, date or size across venture capital (VC funding) of private companies, pre-seed to growth. Who raised money in AI infrastructure this week, who raised a Series A in fintech this week, the largest AI rounds since a date, every round a named fund led or joined. Each funding round carries the company, amount, valuation when stated, lead and other investors, and its sources, so one call answers for many companies' rounds, investors and valuations. Coverage limit: Fireround tracks rounds announced from 2026 onward. It holds a few thousand companies, most of them startups that raised in 2026, and earlier rounds only for some of those. Most companies, and most rounds before 2026, are not on record, so a lookup of an arbitrary company's full funding history, its pre-2026 rounds, an investor's whole portfolio or acquisitions usually returns nothing here; use a company-data provider with historical funding coverage for those.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
